inputs.share_count_basis: FY2025 diluted weighted average (FinStmts FY2025 note 21: 454,685k; no options excluded). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows, buybacks are nil, and the US$4.3bn Antamina/BHP stream was funded with cash, a US$1.5bn term loan and revolver draws -- no equity issued.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash-flow statement share-based compensation add-back (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp 32.504). EquityAwardTaxes 0 in every year: Wheaton's PSUs/RSUs are largely cash-settled, there is no net-share settlement withholding.
inputs.fx_note: USD flows converted to the CAD TSX quote at USD/CAD 1.4254 (Yahoo CAD=X, 2026-10-10T04:21Z). Parity check against the NYSE listing (WPM, USD regular close 2026-10-09): NYSE price x 1.4254 ties to the TSX close within 0.02%, confirming rate, direction and quote basis. Unsuffixed per-share values are CAD; *_usd twins are the flow-currency basis.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD build (flows are USD): US 10y ~4.2% + beta ~0.9 x 5.0% ERP = ~8.7% cost of equity; post-Antamina debt (~US$2.4bn net at closing per FY2025 MD&A) is ~4% of a ~US$63bn market cap at ~5% pre-tax, so WACC ~8.5%. Commodity-price and operator risk are charged in the scenarios (25% bear weight), not as a WACC premium; WACC is identical across scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases ~US$10m undiscounted (FY2025 MD&A contractual obligations) are immaterial (<US$0.03/share) and excluded from both flows and net debt; total_debt is drawn bank debt only (nil at 31-Dec-2025).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (USD flows vs CAD quote; commodity cyclical). Routing: a precious-metals streamer is an operating company whose value is a cash stream, not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco, so owner-FCF is the right row; an asset-by-asset NAV (the sell-side convention for streamers) is not possible from the extracted filings, which give portfolio GEO guidance but not per-stream reserves. The streamer specifics are carried in the drivers: (1) revenue = GEO volume x metal deck, built from management's 860-940k GEO FY2026 guidance and ~1.2M GEO 2030-2035 target, haircut for operator delays; (2) 'capex' is the upfront cash paid to acquire streams -- the committed schedule in the FY2025 MD&A contractual-obligations table (2026 US$587m, 2027-28 US$1,107m, 2029-30 US$146m) plus the US$4.3bn Antamina/BHP upfront payment (closed 1-Apr-2026) charged in FY2026; (3) the terminal year charges a SUSTAINING stream-acquisition capex above depletion, because streams deplete and production only stays flat if Wheaton keeps buying -- 2016-2025 cumulative stream capex of ~US$5.3bn was ~2x cumulative depletion while GEO volumes were roughly flat. BALANCE-SHEET CONVENTION: the anchor is the 31-Dec-2025 balance sheet (net cash US$1,154m, no debt, LTE investments US$410m) and the whole FY2026 is projected, including the Antamina payment; this avoids double-counting H1-2026 cash flow that a post-closing net-debt anchor (~US$2.4bn) would already contain. FY2026 is discounted a full year although ~9 months have elapsed -- a small conservative bias, accepted for consistency with the engine's end-of-year convention. Q1/Q2 2026 filings are not in Extracted/; the FY2026 revenue estimate uses Q2 2026 revenue of US$929m on 209k GEO sold (Analysis.json) plus H2 at spot. Buybacks are nil (non-repurchaser): the flat share count is a modelling convention funded by expensing SBC. TAX: Wheaton's Cayman streams are subject to the 15% global minimum tax (Pillar Two) from 2024; cash payment lags the accrual (FY2024 GMT US$113m and FY2025 US$247-252m sit in taxes payable at 31-Dec-2025, payable in 2026 and 2027), so the cash rate starts low (~5% FY2026, ~11% FY2027) and steps to ~15-15.5% -- the FY2025 cash tax of US$3.6m is NOT a repeatable rate. One-offs excluded from bases: FY2025 US$86m gain on disposal of stream interests; FY2018/2021/2022 disposal gains and impairment reversals.

equity_bridge.item: Long-term equity investments (common shares held) at fair value
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 FinStmts balance sheet / note 16. Not in the flows (FVOCI, no income). US$323m of these were sold in 2026 to help fund Antamina -- the proceeds are this same asset, so it is counted once here.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 8.7% diverges >30% from revenue (16.1%) and EPS (23.5%) 5yr CAGRs. Revenue/EPS growth is mostly metal-price driven (realized price per GEO US$2,426 FY2024 -> US$3,554 FY2025) and is not a forward growth rate; the forward path is built from GEO guidance x a metal deck instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 748.6, FY2022 563.6, FY2025 495.6. FCF CAGRs are negative and meaningless as a trend because 'capex' is lumpy stream acquisition (FY2015 US$1.8bn, FY2018 US$1.1bn, FY2025 US$1.3bn, FY2026 >US$4.8bn incl. Antamina). Owner FCF CAGR sits below reported FCF CAGR (-7.9% vs -5.9% 5yr) because SBC and interest income on the growing cash pile both rose.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 ~US$3,650m: Q1 ~US$0.9bn + Q2 US$929m + H2 ~440k GEO at ~US$4,000/GEO (spot gold ~US$4,200, silver ~US$61). 2027+ holds the current spot deck flat in nominal terms (an implicit real decline) and grows sold GEOs ~5%/yr to ~1.05M by 2030 = management's 1.2M target with a ~10% delay haircut. 2031-35 production held flat per guidance; 1.5% growth is price inflation only. FY2027 dips because the FY2026 average price was above today's spot.
base.margin_rationale: Adj. EBITDA pre-SBC FY2025 82.9% (1,886.8 EBITDA + 32.5 SBC on 2,314.6). Fixed per-ounce payments (~US$514/GEO FY2025) dilute at higher prices, offset by the Antamina/BHP stream's 20%-of-spot payment; ~84% at the spot deck.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 = US$4,300m Antamina/BHP + US$587m committed 2026 payments (Spring Valley 260, Kone 156, El Domo 88, Marmato 82) ~ US$4,900m. 2027-28 = ~US$553m/yr committed (Santo Domingo, Copper World, Spring Valley, Marathon, Cangrejos, El Domo). 2029-30 residual commitments + Salobo CPF ~3%. 2031-34 8%: post-2030 commitments plus the start of replacement deal flow needed to hold 1.2M GEO beyond 2035. Terminal year 18% = depletion (~16%) plus the reinvestment needed to grow at 2% -- a streamer that stops buying is a liquidating annuity.
base.tax_rationale: Cash GMT lags accrual ~2 years (FY2024 paid 2026, FY2025 paid 2027); steady state 15% GMT plus small Canadian tax.
base.narrative: Gold and silver hold today's spot in nominal terms; the development pipeline delivers ~90% of management's 1.2M GEO 2030 target a little late; Antamina/BHP performs; Wheaton keeps buying streams at roughly the rate production depletes.

bull.narrative: Gold rebuilds to ~US$5,000 and silver to ~US$85 by 2028 (the structural bid from central banks and de-dollarisation persists); the pipeline delivers the full 1.2M GEO on time (Salobo CPF accelerated to H1 2028, Blackwater Phase 2, Platreef, Kone, Goose ramp); the expanded US$2.5bn revolver funds further accretive deals that carry growth at ~3% after 2030.

bear.narrative: Metal prices mean-revert from record levels -- gold to ~US$3,200 and silver to ~US$40 by 2028 as real rates rise and the geopolitical premium fades; operator problems at the concentrated cornerstones (Penasquito labour/community disputes, Salobo grades, Peru politics at Antamina) and pre-development delays (Santo Domingo, Copper World, Spring Valley) cut 2030 volume ~20% below target; the committed upfront payments are still made, and the FY2028 cash tax pays the high-price FY2026 GMT on a lower base.

scenario_narratives.base: Spot metals held flat in nominal terms; ~1.05M GEO sold by 2030 (90% of the 1.2M target); Antamina/BHP performs; sustaining stream purchases at ~depletion-plus-growth in the terminal year. The axes are the metal deck, pipeline delivery and the price Wheaton must pay for replacement streams.
scenario_narratives.bull: Gold ~US$5,000 / silver ~US$85, full 1.2M GEO on schedule, and continued accretive deal-making carrying ~3% growth after 2030 with a lower sustaining-capex burden.
scenario_narratives.bear: Gold ~US$3,200 / silver ~US$40 by 2028, ~20% volume shortfall from operator concentration and project delays, committed payments still made, margins compress toward ~79.5%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% house default because gold and silver sit near record levels (silver's 52-week range spans ~US$46-121) and Wheaton's cash flow is ~100% levered to them, with heavy concentration in three operator-controlled mines. Base 50% as the spot-deck, slightly-delayed-pipeline case. Bull cut to 25% because it needs higher metals, on-time delivery and accretive deals all at once.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the stream portfolio as a cash annuity that must be refilled: committed upfront payments (including the US$4.3bn Antamina/BHP stream) are charged as they fall due, the explicit years follow management's GEO guidance with a delay haircut, and the terminal year pays sustaining stream-acquisition capex above depletion. Metals are held at today's spot in the base case rather than at management's higher US$4,800/US$80 deck. Risk sits in the scenarios, not the WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: Metal deck: every US$100/oz on gold moves revenue ~2-3%; the base holds spot flat nominal, below management's US$4,800 gold / US$80 silver planning deck
Terminal sustaining capex: the 18% of revenue base charge (depletion plus growth reinvestment) is the single largest judgement; at depletion-only (~16%) value rises modestly
Pipeline delivery to 1.2M GEO by 2030 depends on development assets operated by third parties (Kone, Platreef, Santo Domingo, Copper World, Spring Valley)
Global minimum tax: cash rate steps from near-zero to ~15% as the lagged Pillar Two payments start in 2026-27
FY2026 discounted a full year although ~9 months have passed (small conservative bias); Q1/Q2 2026 filings not extracted, FY2026 revenue partly estimated
